# e2a runbooks

> Runnable examples of AI agents with authenticated email inboxes, organized by framework and use case.

## Canonical project

- Repository: https://github.com/tokencanopy/e2a-runbooks
- Product: https://e2a.dev
- e2a gives an agent a real email address, verified inbound mail, threaded replies, and optional human approval before outbound delivery.

## Use cases

- Support and escalation agents: https://github.com/tokencanopy/e2a-runbooks/tree/main/mastra
- Multi-agent support routing: https://github.com/tokencanopy/e2a-runbooks/tree/main/crewai
- AI receptionist and front-desk handoffs: https://github.com/tokencanopy/e2a-runbooks/tree/main/openai-agents
- Scheduling agents: https://github.com/tokencanopy/e2a-runbooks/tree/main/pydantic-ai
- Procurement and supplier follow-up: https://github.com/tokencanopy/e2a-runbooks/tree/main/langgraph
- Contract and document review: https://github.com/tokencanopy/e2a-runbooks/tree/main/langchain
- SRE and alert triage: https://github.com/tokencanopy/e2a-runbooks/tree/main/claude-agent-sdk
- Ecommerce and order-support agents: https://github.com/tokencanopy/e2a-runbooks/tree/main/ecommerce

## What the examples teach

- Verify webhook signatures on the raw request bytes.
- Only invoke the agent for `email.received` events.
- Treat inbound email and attachments as untrusted input.
- Pass SPF/DKIM/DMARC authentication evidence into the agent context.
- Claim webhook event ids before running the agent because delivery is at-least-once.
- Use infrastructure-level approval gates for outbound mail.
- Keep examples synthetic and do not use them as production deployments without replacing the documented shortcuts.

## Contribution

To add an example, create a self-contained directory, pin dependencies, document configuration and deployment, use synthetic addresses, add a row to `README.md`, and map the example to a concrete use case.
